description:
Something a competitor actually did, recorded on the day somebody noticed it. A price cut, a block bought, a packing line built, a buyer signed, a shed shut.

WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH A RECORD RATHER THAN A CONVERSATION is that moves only mean anything in sequence. One competitor dropping price is weather; the same competitor dropping price in three consecutive Julys is a strategy, and nobody sees the pattern from memory. So the observation date, the source and the confidence are all stored — a move somebody heard at the co-op counter and a move read in a filing are both worth having and are not worth the same.

THE RESPONSE HALF IS DELIBERATELY SEPARATE FROM THE OBSERVATION HALF. What was recommended, what was actually done, when, and how it turned out — kept apart so the gap between recommended and actual stays visible. That gap is the most instructive thing in the register.
